protections: P1 (present, safe path only): SafeConstructor registers construct_undefined as the fallback constructor, so SafeLoader/safe_load reject every unrecognised tag including all tag:yaml.org,2002:python/* tags (lib3/yaml/constructor.py:411-414,464-465; lib3/yaml/__init__.py:88-102).

P2 (absent): there is no FullConstructor/FullLoader in the pinned tree, hence none of the CVE-2020-1747 state-key-filtering protection exists (lib3/yaml/loader.py:2,31; lib3/yaml/constructor.py:13,157,467).

P3 (absent): yaml.load and yaml.load_all default to the unsafe full Constructor, which registers python/name:, python/module:, python/object:, python/object/apply: and python/object/new: with no validation (lib3/yaml/__init__.py:65,76; lib3/yaml/loader.py:31; lib3/yaml/constructor.py:667-685).

P4 (absent): nothing constrains the callable, args, kwds, state, listitems or dictitems used by construct_python_object_apply; make_python_instance calls whatever object find_python_name resolved (lib3/yaml/constructor.py:546-556,581-614).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: yaml.load defaulting to the unsafe Loader is the documented 4.1 API (announcement.msg:71-73; README:15) and the advisory's FullLoader does not exist in this tree, so a solver can argue the report is inapplicable here.
load_all is the rarely used sibling of load and the advisory names yaml.load/full_load; a fix applied only to load() leaves the identical default here.
The route is only reachable through the explicitly unsafe Loader, which 4.1 documents as the object-construction API, and the FullLoader that CVE-2020-14343 concerns is not present in this tree.
Applying state to an already-created instance looks like ordinary unpickling and there is no blacklist anywhere in this tree, so the state path can be dismissed as not being the reported issue.

python/name: and python/module: are documented round-trip tags that only resolve names and are exercised by the project's own tests, so blocking them looks like a compatibility break rather than a security fix.
listitems/dictitems are required to round-trip list and dict subclasses and are covered by the project's own tests, so a rule that rejects them breaks a must-keep-working value.

The short sequence form and the mapping form reach the same call; a check written against the visible args key of the mapping form silently misses the bare-sequence shape, and the sequence form is how !!python/object/apply is normally written.

conflicts.what: Making yaml.load safe by default (closing T1) rejects the same !!python/object state tags that the recursive round-trip test loads through the default loader (tests/lib3/test_recursive.py:33-35; tests/data/recursive-state.recursive:1-2), so T4's sink cannot simply be refused on the default path.

A guard that refuses non-class callables in make_python_instance closes the os.system/eval routes but does not stop instance.extend/__setitem__ on an attacker-chosen class (lib3/yaml/constructor.py:610,613); conversely blocking listitems/dictitems breaks tests/data/construct-python-object.data:20-21.

Blocking python/name: to cut eval gadget chains also removes the legitimate !!python/name: round-trip emitted by the representer (lib3/yaml/representer.py:288; tests/data/construct-python-name-module.data:1-5).

fairness_risks: The project's own round-trip tests dump and load arbitrary Python objects through the default yaml.load (tests/lib3/test_recursive.py:33-35; tests/data/recursive-state.recursive:1-2), so a rule rejecting !!python/object* on the default path contradicts in-repo must-keep-working behaviour.
Legitimate !!python/object/apply/new usage for classes, immutable types and dict/list subclasses is asserted by tests/data/construct-python-object.data:4-21.

python/name: and python/module: are emitted by the representer for functions and modules (lib3/yaml/representer.py:284-292,359) and round-trip through tests/data/construct-python-name-module.data:1-5.
YAMLObject subclasses default to yaml_loader = Loader (lib3/yaml/__init__.py:292), so a safe default loader breaks application classes that rely on plain yaml.load.
Passing Loader=Loader or Loader=CLoader explicitly is documented (README:15-16; lib3/yaml/cyaml.py:28) and must keep working.

design.why: Against the pinned code the best stack is T1/T2 (unsafe default on both module entry points), T3/T7 (arbitrary callable through both shapes of python/object/apply), T4 (unrestricted python/object state application), T5 (python/name+python/module resolution) and T6 (listitems/dictitems side effects): five independent fix sites with five different dismissal reasons (documented 4.1 behaviour; only reachable via the unsafe Loader; state looks like normal unpickling; name/module are legitimate round-trip tags; listitems are required for list/dict subclasses). T1/T3/T4 hit DeepSeek's absent-protection-with-a-reason-to-dismiss weakness and T6 hits MiMo's coupled-value weakness, so the mix beats a design centred on python/object/apply alone (one guard, one judgement). It is not, however, the H3b1 pair: this checkout is PyYAML 4.1, predates the CVE-2020-1747 fix entirely, and has no FullLoader/FullConstructor for CVE-2020-14343 to be an incomplete fix of.
